implementation_state: Warmup is a pure library entry point: it takes a canonical dataset snapshot, projects it once at the training boundary, trains the four per-dimension models through the accepted fallible seam, and returns a verified ModelCommit with complete root-to-commit lineage plus an honest report. It installs nothing, runs on no schedule, and is unreachable from the running product. Accepted on dev at a332b79.
unblock_condition: Accepted: deterministic output, verifiable lineage, a holdout disjoint by construction, an honest improvement verdict that cannot be claimed on a degenerate holdout, and no reachable activation path.
notes: This is the first node that consumes the collected dataset, and the first that trains anything at all. Training happened here; activation did not and may not.

The worker's commit arrived with no subject line at all, so the message began at Why: and violated the commit contract. The parent rewrote the subject on integration; the three source files were already bit-identical to the worker's tree, so only the message changed.

The dispatch brief asserted two facts about the seam that were both wrong: try_train_with_history is private rather than returning a lineage, and try_train_and_swap does not exist while ShadowEngine::swap plus ShadowEngine::try_train is the real activation surface. The worker verified both instead of trusting them.

The typed contract participates only as a load-and-score attestation. A training row has no representation in ModelInput, DecisionCandidate, or DecisionState, so adding a training method there would be the wrong fix.

FOLLOW-UP OWNED BY 7B, recorded rather than hidden: validate_outcome_sample enforces the non-success timing discipline for request scope only, so an attempt-scope sample can carry latency_ms or ttft_ms with success false. Warmup closes this locally with WarmupError::NonSuccessTiming, but the gap is still in the accepted dataset validator.

Determinism is scoped to the four ModelState payloads, the commit id, the checkpoint content hash, and the report. ModelCheckpoint::created_at and FrozenHoldout::frozen_at are wall-clock and are excluded from the claim.

A Better verdict requires strictly lower log loss and no Brier regression, and is withheld entirely when the holdout holds one class, because the cold baseline answering p=0.5 makes any base-rate learner look like an improvement on such a holdout.
No bandit or RL (7E-2C), no calibration (7E-2D), no durable journal (7E-2E), and no snapshot or activation machinery (7E-2F) belongs here.
